interpretation: The release covers 2 monthly period(s) (2026-04-01 to 2026-05-01). Cross-sectional comparisons are supported; trends in usage composition are not.

Model counts fall monotonically from 2025 to 2026, which is consistent with curation lag and also with a genuine slowdown. The two cannot be distinguished from this dataset, so release-count trends are not published for these years.
The most recent public submission is dated 2025-12-15, 224 days before the reference date. The leaderboard supports historical statements only; it cannot describe current agent capability.
Usage composition is measured for one vendor's products. It describes who uses that product and how, and carries no information about the workforce or about employment outcomes.
Training compute (FLOP) is disclosed for 39.1% of models. Any statistic conditioned on this field describes disclosing models, which are not a random sample.
Training dataset size is disclosed for 39.3% of models. Any statistic conditioned on this field describes disclosing models, which are not a random sample.
Training hardware is disclosed for 33.2% of models. Any statistic conditioned on this field describes disclosing models, which are not a random sample.

24.4% of models have no usable accessibility class, either because the field is empty or because the accessibility statement and the open-weights flag disagree. These rows are excluded from open-versus-closed comparisons rather than assigned to the closed side.

17,855 rows (0.94%) share a model, category and publication date with at least one other row carrying a different rating. They are combined by inverse-variance weighting with the between-replicate spread added to the standard error. Taking a maximum instead would bias affected models upward by tens of rating points.

The rating system changed on 2024-01-09 (Elo to Bradley-Terry), 2025-05-16 (style control by default) and 2025-07-23 (frequency re-weighting). Trends are estimated within a single regime; a slope spanning a break would partly measure the methodology change.
A vendor-published quality index exists for 31.4% of listed models. Price-versus-quality statements describe that subset, which skews toward prominent models.

44 of 341 listed models charge more above a prompt-length threshold. Reading only the base rate understates long-context cost, so price tables report the base rate and the rate at 64,000 prompt tokens separately.

A submission measures an agent scaffold together with a model. Directory names are author-chosen, so the underlying model cannot always be identified. Scores are attributed to systems, never to models alone.
Parameter count is disclosed for 64.9% of models. Any statistic conditioned on this field describes disclosing models, which are not a random sample.
Accessibility statement is disclosed for 75.6% of models. Any statistic conditioned on this field describes disclosing models, which are not a random sample.
5.8% of arena rows carry a licence string this project cannot classify as open or proprietary. They are excluded from the open-versus-closed frontier rather than assumed closed.
7 listings carry an expiration date. This is direct evidence of the catalogue turnover that makes the cross-section unusable as a price history.
Some listings expose no usable completion price, typically non-text models. They are excluded from price statistics.
